A communication system will be implemented to enable an external communication for the MTV. This communication will monitor and control the MTV remotely and create a database backup of the most relevant data. This communication will be composed of a 5G/4G antenna and a VPN router, which Final Technical Report 36/57 creates a VPN tunnel through the internet to connect the MTV with an onshore station most securely. In addition, a redundant internet connection will be provided through a dedicated satellite modem and antenna. This last option enables external connections at almost every point in the world when the main means are unavailable. In the communication system, there will also be a WIFI access point to extend the LAN network a few hundred feet around the MTV, which will be used for MTV operation from close proximity. A wireless HMI would also be provided and implemented to control the systems and perform maintenance more easily while having free movement. The MODAQ will be implemented in the MTV as a database storage in the initial deployment phase. It will store all the data collected and processed locally by the Integrated Control System and remotely in the Amazon Web Services Cloud. Additionally, further functionalities may be implemented in subsequent phases. Some of these are installing several sensors that enable the possibility of performing accredited tests. For those turbines that are provided without any controller, the MODAQ can be equipped with all the necessary equipment to control and monitor the turbine. Final Technical Report 37/57 10 ELECTRICAL SYSTEM DESIGN The MTV electrical system design gathers the MTV pure-vessel systems and equipment, similar to traditional vessels, as well as the CEC electrical system associated with the testing capabilities of the vessel. The design of the electrical system is divided into two main sections: the MTV vessel electrical system and the CEC test system. The first one describes the design of the onboard electrical system, which is designed to maintain the vessel's operability and provide the necessary power to the general equipment, such as general interior and exterior lighting, electrical winches, electrical motors, pumps, etc. CEC electrical test system describes the design of the electrical system to provide an electrical infrastructure for allowing CEC to be tested in real conditions. 10.1 MTV Vessel Electrical System The MTV onboard electrical system (Figure 10-1) is designed to power all the main functions of the vessel. Various subsystems are incorporated to maintain the vessel’s operability as needed and per general design standards. The system is a 480 V (3-phase) based diesel generator-powered system with an additional 120 V (1-phase) proposed for auxiliary purposes. A lithium-ion battery-based UPS system is incorporated for emergency power supply. The electrical balance has been analyzed to estimate the power demand on the vessel under five distinct operating scenarios. Figure 10-1 MTV onboard electrical system outline Final Technical Report
